newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan decides to hold long-delayed census.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan decides to hold long-delayed census.

text.p: The Pakistani government decided in principle on Wednesday to hold the first national population census since 1981, a government official said.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's adviser on information and culture Mushahid Hussain told a news conference the cabinet had told the Statistics Division to prepare for the census.
Plans to hold the census have been postponed three times in the past following disputes in Pakistan's four provinces.
Hussain said Sharif had asked provincial chief ministers to submit their views. No date has been fixed for the census.
Pakistan's population, believed to be growing at a rapid 2.9 to three percent a year, was officially estimated at 131.45 million in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June).
The 1981 census put the population at 84 million.
